prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks, which trap atoms at a magic wavelength and have brought frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: Optical lattice clocks have a clear before and after. Katori's magic-wavelength idea removes the light shift that would otherwise ruin spectroscopy of trapped atoms, so that many atoms can be interrogated at once without a Doppler or recoil penalty. Ye's group took the concept to the 10^-18 level and used it to study many-body coherence and clock comparisons. Independent laboratories in Japan, the USA, France, Germany and China have built such clocks and compared them, and the agreement at this level is reproduced rather than claimed by a single group. The clocks have also produced new physics. They resolve the gravitational redshift over millimetre scales, they constrain drifts of constants, and they are the basis of the coming redefinition of the second. The two-name credit is clean and covers the decisive concept and its realisation at the state of the art. It also sits in a coherent line of recognition, since the frequency comb was honoured in 2005 and ion control in 2012, and it is distinct from both.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that this is a refinement of metrology that has already been honoured twice, in 2005 for the comb and in 2012 for ion control, and that a committee may want a discovery of something unexpected in nature rather than a better instrument. I also have a mild bias towards atomic structure and precision measurement, since this is my own field, so I should not overweight it. Other names such as Lemonde, Takamoto and Derevianko have claims on specific steps (theory of the shifts, early demonstrations, comparisons), and the second has not yet been formally redefined. Finally, the quantum-boundary physics I find most compelling in the 2025 prize is stronger in B013 than in a clock, though B013 is less mature and has diffuse credit.

responses.point: Ulf ranks the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators (B004) first, as a genuine discovery with a clear before and after that is confirmed by many groups, and he places the lattice clock fifth because of overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
responses.response: I agree that B004 is a deep conceptual discovery, and it is my own third choice. I do not think the overlap objection is as strong for the clocks as you make it. The comb gave the ruler and ion control gave a different clock, whereas the magic-wavelength lattice is a new way of interrogating thousands of atoms, with a distinct physical idea behind it and a distinct set of results, including millimetre-scale redshifts. My real difficulty with B004 is attribution, which you flag yourself. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe realisation that Molenkamp observed, and Hasan's three-dimensional work cannot fit in a three-person prize. Kane, Mele and Molenkamp would also stand close to the 2016 recognition of topology in matter. If the committee can settle the credit, I would not object to B004 as a strong alternative, but today the clock case is cleaner.

responses.point: Goran ranks circuit QED (B028) first as a clean foundational demonstration of strong light-matter coupling on a chip that underlies superconducting processors, and he openly flags his own closeness to credited people and to the Chalmers community.
responses.response: I appreciate that Goran declared his proximity, and I think it is right that he weigh how much to push B028 himself. On the science, circuit QED is excellent and replicated everywhere, but two things hold me back. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits is very close in subject, and returning to the same community within a year seems poor timing. The four-name credit (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Girvin) also forces an exclusion that Olle, Stefan and Eva O. each resolve differently, which shows that the allocation is not settled. I rank it below the clocks for those reasons, not for lack of merit. I would also say that the Cirac-Zoller theory that you rank second is attractive and clean, but I see it as the less urgent call because the experimental side was honoured in 2012.

responses.point: Olle ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B017) first, as a theory prediction followed by an experimental discovery that opened moire quantum materials, and he regards the matter as timely and the field as reproduced widely.
responses.response: The prediction-then-discovery structure is exactly what I like, and the correlated insulator and superconductivity results have been reproduced by many groups. My hesitation is maturity, which you also raise: the pairing mechanism is unresolved and the phase diagram is still moving. The prize would then rest partly on an open interpretation, and I am sceptical when the headline phenomenon still lacks a settled explanation. I also note the three-name question (Bistritzer or not) is real. Defer to you and Bernhard on whether the condensed matter community regards the core discovery as stable enough, but I would rather see this a few years later than now.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee gives to a metrology achievement relative to the discovery of a new phenomenon, given the 2005 and 2012 AMO prizes.
Whether the citation should name the lattice clock alone or also acknowledge ion clocks or the comb, and whether Lemonde, Takamoto or others deserve a mention in the text.
Whether a three-person B004 configuration can be made fair when Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Hasan are outside the credited names.
I rely on memory for exact accuracy records and the dates of the first lattice-clock demonstrations.
statement.conflict_note: I am a long-time close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and have worked with the Lund and ETH attosecond groups, but none of the credited names on B041 (Katori, Ye) is a collaborator, so no specific conflict is apparent for my preferred candidate. I have no stated tie to Cirac, Zoller or the other shortlisted candidates in my profile, although I know many people in the AMO community and a committee secretary may wish to confirm that no recusal is needed for B002, B034 and B042.
